paragraphs: “Pious man”: R. Yehudah ben Bava; see R. Yehudah bar Ilai. Shabbat 150b: a caper bush grew. There, 127b: a pious man redeemed a girl. Berakhot 18b: a pious man heard young women conversing, described in the Bavli as two spirits in a cemetery. Shekalim: he dug wells. Ein Omdin, Berakhot 32b, near the end: he did not return a certain official's greeting. Yuchasin, in its introduction, writes that these were called pious: Yosi ben Yoezer, R. Yosi the priest, R. Yehudah ben Bava, R. Yehudah bar Ilai, Hillel, Bava ben Buti, R. Akiva, Shmuel the Younger, Shimon the Pious, King David, and Ezra. End of quotation. Nedarim 10a: the earlier pious men longed to bring a sin-offering, etc.
